## Example 2.15 {#fv2-example-2-15 .fv-lesson .proof-lesson }

```{=html}
<p>The position vectors of the points <span data-math="P"></span>, <span data-math="Q"></span>, <span data-math="R"></span>, and <span data-math="S"></span> are respectively</p><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="4\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}-\underset{\sim}{k},\quad5\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}+2\underset{\sim}{k}"></span></div><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="2\underset{\sim}{i}-2\underset{\sim}{j}-3\underset{\sim}{k}\quad\text{and}\quad4\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}+3\underset{\sim}{k}"></span></div><p>a) Show that <span data-math="\overrightarrow{PQ}"></span> is parallel to <span data-math="\overrightarrow{RS}"></span></p><p>b) Is <span data-math="PQRS"></span> a parallelogram?</p>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 2.15 · p. 32</div>

::: {.notes}
Source values: P=(4,3,−1), Q=(5,2,2), R=(2,−2,−3), S=(4,−4,3). PQ=(1,−1,3), RS=(2,−2,6)=2PQ, so they are parallel. PQRS is not a parallelogram: these opposite sides have different lengths, |RS|=2|PQ|. Parallelism of one pair is insufficient. Do not confuse equal direction with equal vector.
:::
